name: Earth and Proxima comoving to about one part in 1e4

source.located: No single external source is cited by the tree (ledger.py:2029-2036 states the figure bare; oneway.py:64 carries the one input it has, RV 22.2 km/s, as RECALLED). The measurement rests on Proxima's astrometry: Gaia DR3 parallax 768.0665+-0.0499 mas, proper motion (-3781.741, 769.465) mas/yr, and the HARPS absolute radial velocity -22.204+-0.032 km/s of Kervella, Thevenin & Lovis 2017 (A&A 598, L7; arXiv:1611.03495), plus Earth's orbital speed.

published_statement: Tree (ledger.py:2033-2035, W8): 'Earth and Proxima are comoving to about one part in 1e4, so a receiver at rest in Proxima's atoms automatically shares Earth's B whatever B is.' External measurement restated: Proxima's heliocentric radial velocity -22.204+-0.032 km/s (Kervella et al. 2017, HARPS, corrected for gravitational redshift and convective blueshift); Gaia DR3 parallax 768.0665 mas and proper motion 3.8592 arcsec/yr, hence v_t = 23.82 km/s and |v| = 32.56 km/s relative to the Sun (computed here).
published_hypotheses: H1 (measurement): Proxima's heliocentric space velocity is fixed by parallax, proper motion and an absolute RV (convective-blueshift and gravitational-redshift corrected)
H2 (tree, unstated): 'Earth' means Earth's instantaneous velocity, which includes the 29.78 km/s orbital motion comparable in size to Proxima's heliocentric 32.56 km/s
H3 (tree, unstated): 'receiver at rest in Proxima's atoms' = at rest in the star Proxima's frame, not on Proxima b
H4 (tree, unstated): 'shares B' is a statement about a quantity that transforms multiplicatively (Doppler factor / Lorentz factor / rapidity), not equality of the velocity B itself
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED tolerance (ledger.py:2034-2035): 'automatically shares Earth's B whatever B is' is exact only multiplicatively: for any common boost B the Doppler factor of a fixed null direction seen from Earth and from Proxima differs by a factor in [e^-eta, e^+eta], eta = artanh(beta_rel) <= 2.08e-4 (proved in sympy, checked over B in {1.23e-3, 0.5, 0.999387630, 0.99999993}). In B itself the collinear difference is B'-B = b(1-B^2)/(1+Bb): 1.2e-7 relative at the tree's priced B = 0.999387630 (branelink.py:84), but 8.1 % relative at the CMB-dipole speed the tree names as 'the RECEIVER's B' (branelink.py:74). 'whatever B is' holds for the Doppler-type saving, not for B as a velocity when B ~ beta_rel.

WEAKENED/UNSTATED range (ledger.py:2033-2034): 'about one part in 1e4' is a seasonal range, not a constant: Earth-Proxima relative speed 10.8-62.3 km/s, beta_rel 3.6e-5 .. 2.08e-4 (Earth orbital eccentricity and rotation included). Proxima's heliocentric beta is 1.086e-4. Order of magnitude 1e-4 holds; a factor ~2 above and ~3 below.

UNSTATED receiver site (ledger.py:2034 vs ledger.py:189, which names Proxima b as the condensed body): a receiver on Proxima b adds orbital speed 47.2 km/s (a = 0.0485 AU, P = 11.186 d, RECALLED); worst-case bound beta_rel <= 3.65e-4, still 'a few parts in 1e4'.

NO SOURCE NAMED (ledger.py:2029-2036): the figure is stated bare; the tree's only input, oneway.py:64 PROXIMA_RADIAL_MS = 22.2e3, is marked RECALLED and carries only the radial component (the transverse 23.8 km/s is larger).

rederivation.outcome: Proxima heliocentric |v| = 32.563 km/s (v_t 23.819, v_r -22.204), beta 1.086e-4; velocity at ecliptic latitude 20.27 deg. Earth-Proxima relative speed swept over Earth's orbit (circular and eccentric extremes, rotation +-0.465 km/s): 10.82 .. 62.33 km/s, beta_rel 3.61e-5 .. 2.08e-4. Receiver on Proxima b: <= 3.65e-4. Sympy: Doppler-factor ratio between frames of relative speed b is gamma_b(1 - b mu), whose extremes squared equal e^{-+2 artanh b} exactly (difference simplifies to 0), with no dependence on the common boost; brute-force over random directions at B in {1.23e-3, 0.5, 0.999387630, 0.99999993} gives max |ln ratio|/eta = 0.999823 <= 1. Collinear composition B'-B = b(1-B^2)/(1+Bb): relative 8.1e-2 at B = 1.2336e-3, 1.2e-7 at B = 0.999387630, 1.4e-11 at B = 0.99999993. The priced escape save = T d ((1+B)/(1-B))^2 (branelink.b_for_saving) differs between endpoints by <= e^{4 eta}-1 = 8.3e-4 at any B.

lacked_data: The tree's own input is only the recalled radial component (22.2 km/s, oneway.py:64) and no source; what it lacked was the transverse component (23.8 km/s, the larger one, from Gaia proper motion and parallax) and Earth's 29.8 km/s orbital velocity, which is comparable to Proxima's heliocentric 32.6 km/s. Supplying both (computed here) moves the figure from 'one part in 1e4' to a seasonal range 3.6e-5 .. 2.1e-4 (3.7e-4 bound on Proxima b), which is still 'about 1e-4' in order of magnitude. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this row: the corrected RV revision (-21.700 -> -22.204 km/s) and Gaia-era astrometry move |v_sun| by 0.34 km/s, 1 %; no datum that has moved changes the conclusion. The one quantity that is genuinely missing, the preferred-frame boost B, provably does not enter the Doppler-type comparison (multiplicative bound independent of B). No external author's result is shown wrong; nothing here is a refutation.
grade_evidence: The measurement stands: Earth-Proxima beta_rel = 3.6e-5 .. 2.08e-4 (computed from Gaia DR3 astrometry and the Kervella 2017 RV, both READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT), 'about 1e-4' in order. The consequence 'automatically shares Earth's B whatever B is' holds only with a named tolerance the tree drops: the endpoints' Doppler/Lorentz factors agree to within e^{+-eta}, eta <= 2.1e-4, for every B (sympy-proved), so W8's conclusion -- no joint unsatisfiability, the closure does not stand -- is unaffected (saving spread <= 8.3e-4). But B as a velocity is not shared when B is comparable to beta_rel: 8.1 % relative at the CMB-dipole speed the tree names as the receiver's B (branelink.py:74). Holding on the smaller class (multiplicative quantities, or B >> 1e-4) is NARROWED, not WRONG. Source values are not read at source (alphaXiv quota, arXiv blocked), which is why the grade is not STANDS on the data side either.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: W8 rewritten to 'comoving to beta_rel 3.6e-5 .. 2.1e-4 (seasonal), so the Doppler factor of any common boost B agrees between the endpoints to a factor e^{+-2.1e-4}', and Kervella 2017 / Gaia DR3 read at source confirming -22.204 km/s and the astrometry. To WRONG: only an RV or proper-motion revision of order 30 km/s (hundreds of sigma), or a use of W8 where B as a velocity (not a multiplicative factor) must match at B ~ 1e-3 -- neither is present. To OPEN: if the restated astrometric values were shown not to be Gaia DR3's.
